# .github/workflows/

`ci.yml` runs the `scripts/validate` manifest as individually named steps on every pull request targeting `main`, every merge-queue entry and every push to `main`. It never invokes the runner itself; the runner's own behaviour is covered by `scripts/test-validate.sh`, which continuous integration does run. What it can and cannot reach is [../../scripts/AGENTS.md](../../scripts/AGENTS.md) § What continuous integration covers, and what it cannot.

- The merge queue requires two contexts: `ci-ok`, the one suite job in `ci.yml`, and `Review gate`, a commit status that `review-gate-writer.yml` is the only writer of. Require the writer's **status**, never its job name — the writer job on a pull-request head is a relay, so requiring the evaluating job's name would block every pull request. The live list comes from the repository's rulesets through the GitHub API rather than from a copy here.
- The writer always runs the default branch's engine, so a pull request that repairs the gate machinery can never open its own gate. Merging one is the ruleset bypass actor's job, stated in the merge commit.
- The whitespace check is range-scoped here, because `scripts/validate` lists a working-tree check that would inspect nothing on a clean checkout. There is one defined base per event and deliberately **no fallback base**: an unresolvable base fails the step rather than substituting a narrower range that would pass while claiming coverage it does not have. A whole-tree check is not used, because the tree's pre-existing findings all sit in content VGS ships verbatim.
- A diff whose every path is `kendex refresh` output skips the toolchain-bearing tail of `ci-ok`; the cheap text checks still run tree-wide and `ci-ok` still reports. The predicate is the kendex `harness-ci` package, called from one step, and it is tested upstream — do not propose restoring the lanes for it.
- `publish-aur.yml` pushes the Arch recipes after a packaging change or a tag, re-checks the published result, and **fails rather than skipping** when its credential is absent. `publish-gentoo.yml` publishes nothing: deploy keys are disabled for this organisation by enterprise policy, so the overlay is published by hand and this workflow runs only the credential-free weekly drift check. Both exist because a stale package builds and installs perfectly well, so the failure is silent by construction and something has to look.
- `release.yml` builds releases on version tags. Code scanning runs from the organisation-level default setup rather than a workflow here, and its per-language lanes report as skipped because the repository has little or no code in those languages.

[../../docs/decisions/D007-ci-single-job-economics.md](../../docs/decisions/D007-ci-single-job-economics.md) holds the measured economics behind the single suite job, and the commands to re-measure them: at that scale per-job overhead dominates, so there are no lanes, no nightly run, no Go caching, and a small runner tier.
